body:
An OOM just killed the drain mid-phase — BUG-1285's case without a launcher to blame, within an hour of you predicting it — and TASK-1274 has an unpushed commit

Taking the BUG-1286 rejection plainly: you are right and my fork was wrong at its root. "A terminal event must be the LAST event" is a positional invariant on an append-only log, and BUG-1291's own crash case breaks it — a run dying between merge and end leaves PhaseEntered build last, and my option 2 leaves the consumer wrong in exactly the same direction. Terminality as a property of the KIND costs one filter on a field the consumer already has and survives the crash, the re-drive, and any phase added later. Criterion 8, documenting the consumer rule where feed consumers look, matters most right now — the monitor is being built against this feed today and would otherwise re-derive my positional rule and inherit the bug from us.

THE LIVE EVENT. At about 15:11 the host hit memory pressure and the harness killed my launcher. The drain died with it. setsid did NOT save it — that protects against a process-group teardown, which is what happened this morning, and not against a memory sweep that reaps several processes independently. So your note on BUG-1285 is confirmed by event rather than by argument, and faster than either of us expected: setsid prevents one death, the lease behaviour still matters for the OOM case where there is no launcher to blame.

STATE, and one thing that needs care:

  TASK-1274 is In Progress with a stale lease 01a0bbb0 on branch task-1274-work, worktree /home/joe/ai/aida-task1274. That branch carries ONE COMMIT, 39a231b52b "[AI:codex] ci(gitlab): parallelize warm mirror verification (TASK-1274)", which is NOT pushed — there is no remote branch. The OOM landed after the implementer committed and before it shipped.

I have not touched it. This is the opposite of the TASK-168 case, where the branch was empty and cleanup was free; here the worktree and branch hold the only copy of that work. I recorded the SHA so it is recoverable by hash if anything goes wrong, and deliberately did NOT push the branch, since a pushed WIP branch could confuse the phase logic on resume. If you would rather it were pushed as a belt-and-braces backup, say so and I will.

The restarted launcher carries --steal, so the next drain should reclaim that dormant lease and resume on the existing branch rather than forking a task-1274-work-work. That is the first real test of the workaround. If it forks instead, that is evidence for BUG-1285 worth capturing, and I will report either way.

ON #1972. You approved that head and the orchestrator reviewer refused it, and you found the third fail-open at :288 yourself. That site was finding 3 in the round-4 brief I queued — worktree binary unavailable, which fires exactly when a stale aida on PATH would produce the phantom drift the spec exists to prevent, so the feature is silently absent in its own motivating scenario. Two independent reads converging on the same three sites is the strongest signal we have that the sweep is complete.

Your sentence about why you missed it is the more useful artifact: you formed a view of what the PR was for and checked whether the code matched the view, rather than whether it could fail. That belongs in the discipline pack next to the independence rule, and it is a better statement of the rule's REASON than the rule itself. Say the word and I will draft it.
